summary: Portage Island's 1869 range light, moved in 1986 from the island to a boardwalk by the Shippagan aquarium, New Brunswick.

light.characteristic: fixed white catoptric light to 1909; occulting white, 7 s light and 2 s eclipse from 1909 (1909 report)

structures.note: On Portage Island until 1986, then rebuilt at Shippagan (LF; Digest). Height 43 ft per Tourism New Brunswick.
Chance anchor lens lantern on a pole 27 ft high. LF dates it 1908; the Department's report for the twelve months to 31 March 1909 records it.

access.note: On a public boardwalk near the New Brunswick Aquarium and Marine Centre in Shippagan. LF: grounds open, tower closed. Lighthouse Digest: open to the public.

facts.agency: New Brunswick Department of Tourism and Parks

events.note: Work began September 1869; light first exhibited 6 October 1869. Lantern room and four silvered reflectors came from Point Escuminac (LF).
Original buildings cost $604.40; no title to the land had been secured (LF).
Keeper's dwelling completed May 1872 was destroyed by fire in February 1875 (LF).
Breakwater put in place to stop the sea encroaching on the station (LF).
Front range mast light placed on the south end of the island. LF says 1908; the Department's report for the year to 31 March 1909 records it (conflict noted).
Old fixed white catoptric light replaced by a 4th order dioptric occulting white light in a new lantern (1909 report).
New keeper's dwelling built on the island (LF).
Tower dismantled in three pieces, carried by boat to Burnt Church and rebuilt on a wharf in Shippagan near the aquarium (LF; Tourism NB).
Lighthouse Digest gives the deactivation as c. 1986.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: LF and Tourism NB date the tower to 1869; Lighthouse Digest gives 'Date Present Tower Built: 1908'. The Department's report for 1909 describes a new lantern and a front mast light, not a new tower, so the 1869 date stands for the tower and 1908 for the mast. The Digest entry is not reconciled.
LF says grounds open, tower closed, and the lantern room is now empty. Lighthouse Digest says the tower is open to the public. The sources disagree; the story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Keeper names and dates before 1900 come only from LighthouseFriends: the Department's reports for those years are not in the local corpus, which starts in 1900. Peter Morrison, Jr. is confirmed from 1892 only by the 1901 statement. Matches of names to stations in the OCR statement were made on the same printed line, so no column-position matching. Dates conflict: LF and Tourism NB give 1869 for the tower, while Lighthouse Digest gives 'Date Present Tower Built: 1908'; the 1909 report's mast is recorded as 1908 by LF and as the year to 31 March 1909 by the Department. Last keeper year: LF 'at least 1961', Tourism NB 'until 1960'. Gratten/Gratton spelling. Tourism NB and LF disagree on the visitor centre's status. The Vickers column is paywalled after the first section; only that section was read. No storms or wrecks tied to the station were found in the annual reports read, so the chapter is omitted. The record's ownership field ('federal') is a proposed correction, not applied. Fact-check 2026-10-28: the story was revised. The Vickers author is now described only as writing in a Northumberland Free Press Substack post, since the source gives no columnist title. The reflector sentence no longer infers a cause from the lantern history. The 1876 inspector is no longer called the same inspector as 1875. The Digest's 'Date Present Tower Built: 1908' is now stated in the story as an unresolved disagreement with the 1869 date. The 1909 report pages (mast light printed p. 57; new light printed p. 72) and the 1901 statement page (printed p. 128) were confirmed through corpus.py page labels, with no column matching. The Tourism NB and Digest access conflict is stated, and the visit advice now says not to enter unless confirmed open.
